summary: Lebanon issues free one-month visas on arrival at Beirut airport to citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia and many other countries — extendable to three months — while GCC nationals enter visa-free; other nationalities need a visa from a Lebanese embassy or prior approval from General Security, and Canada says travelers with evidence of travel to Israel may be refused entry.

notes: Canada's travel advice says travel to or from Israel is illegal in Lebanon, and that you may be refused entry if your passport bears an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian stamp from a crossing that borders Israel.

payments.text: The UK says Lebanon's prolonged economic crisis may affect paying by card, that many companies do not accept credit or debit cards, and that US dollars are widely accepted and the main cash currency. Canada calls the economy mainly cash-based, says foreign currency can be exchanged at licensed exchange bureaus but not at banks, and that some banks limit daily ATM withdrawals.

safety.text: Airstrikes and rocket fire between Israel and Hizballah escalated from 2 March; a cessation of hostilities was announced in June 2026, but fighting and airstrikes continue, particularly in the south. The FCDO advises against all travel to the South and Nabatiyeh governorates, parts of Beirut's southern suburbs, eastern Beqaa, northern Baalbek-Hermel and Akkar, and the Palestinian refugee camps, and against all but essential travel to several other areas. The FCDO says Beirut airport is open and operational.

tips.text: Evidence of travel to Israel can lead to refused entry. Canada's travel advice says this includes an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian stamp from a crossing that borders Israel, and that travel to or from Israel is illegal in Lebanon.
Canada advises against all travel to Lebanon and says airstrikes could resume, mostly in southern Lebanon, Beirut's southern suburbs, the Beqaa Valley and Palestinian refugee camps.
The UK says US dollars are widely accepted and the main cash currency, that many companies do not accept credit or debit cards, and advises having access to enough cash for your stay.

The UK says Lebanon's power plants produce only limited electricity for the national grid, which can lead to power cuts, that many businesses rely heavily on generators, and advises having a torch to hand at night; Canada says power outages and electricity rationing are common, including in Beirut.
The free one-month visa on arrival can be extended to three months at a General Security office.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lebanon?
faq.answer: Most Western travelers do not need to arrange anything in advance: citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and many other countries receive a free one-month visa on arrival at Beirut airport, extendable to three months. GCC nationals enter visa-free. Other nationalities need a visa from a Lebanese embassy or prior approval from General Security before travel.

faq.question: Can I enter Lebanon if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says travel to or from Israel is illegal in Lebanon and that you may be refused entry if your passport bears an Israeli visa or border stamp, or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp from a crossing that borders Israel; the UK says an Israeli stamp can lead to refusal even with a valid Lebanese visa.

faq.question: Is Lebanon safe to visit right now?
faq.answer: Canada advises against all travel to Lebanon. It says the security situation remains volatile, that missiles and drones have struck targets in the country, and that airstrikes could resume, mostly in southern Lebanon, Beirut's southern suburbs, the Beqaa Valley and Palestinian refugee camps.

faq.question: How much does the Lebanese visa on arrival cost?
faq.answer: Nothing — the standard one-month single-entry tourist visa issued on arrival at Beirut airport is free for eligible nationalities. Extensions to three months are handled by General Security in Lebanon.

faq.question: What money should I bring to Lebanon?
faq.answer: US dollars in cash. The UK says US dollars are widely accepted and the main cash currency, and that the economic crisis may affect paying by card; Canada says the economy is mainly cash-based and that dollars can be exchanged at licensed exchange bureaus, not at banks.
